title: Bias library (1): loss aversion, herd, recency, anchoring
objectives: Recognise loss aversion, herd/FOMO, recency and anchoring from client quotes.
Answer each with the manual's “what to say” line.
body_md:
Loss aversion: losses hurt about twice as much as equal gains please. Sounds like: “The market fell, let me stop my SIP.” Say: “Your SIP is buying more units cheaper now. Stopping skips the best buying opportunity.” Herd / FOMO: following what everyone else is doing. Sounds like: “Everyone is buying small-caps.” Say: “Let's check it fits your allocation first. Popular usually means it has already run up.” Recency: over-weighting the latest results. Sounds like: “This fund gave 40% last year.” Say: “Let's look at its 5-year record and how it did in bad years.” Anchoring: fixating on a reference number like the buy price. Sounds like: “I'll sell once it's back to my cost.” Say: “Your buying price doesn't affect what the fund does next. Is it still right for you?”

| Bias | What it is | How it sounds | What to say |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Loss aversion | Losses hurt about twice as much as equal gains please | "The market fell, let me stop my SIP." | "Your SIP is buying more units cheaper now. Stopping skips the best buying opportunity." |
| Herd / FOMO | Following what everyone else is doing | "Everyone is buying small-caps." | "Let's check it fits your allocation first. Popular usually means it has already run up." |
| Recency | Over-weighting the latest results | "This fund gave 40% last year." | "Let's look at its 5-year record and how it did in bad years." |
| Anchoring | Fixating on a reference number like the buy price | "I'll sell once it's back to my cost." | "Your buying price doesn't affect what the fund does next. Is it still right for you?" |
example: “This fund gave 40% last year” → recency: look at the 5-year record and how it did in bad years.
say: Your SIP is buying more units cheaper now.
Popular usually means it has already run up.
never: Sell the winner, keep the loser, always.
Last year's return is the reason to invest.

check.q: Is knowing about biases enough to stop them affecting decisions?
o: No — knowing doesn't switch them off; systems and habits do
check.why: Knowing doesn't switch them off; systems and habits do.

check.q: “I'll sell once it's back to my cost” is:
check.why: Anchoring: fixating on a reference number like the buy price. Say: “Your buying price doesn't affect what the fund does next.”
Herd / FOMO: following what everyone else is doing. Say: “Let's check it fits your allocation first.”
